name: Doze and idle mode
plain: When the phone is still and unplugged, Android delays jobs, alarms and network to save battery.
meaning: Explains why background trackers go quiet at night. Apps get brief maintenance windows; only high priority push, exact alarms and foreground services run freely.

android.prompt_ui: Settings > Battery > Unrestricted removes the app from optimization
android.persistence: Doze deepens over hours; maintenance windows get longer
android.store_policy: Play: ignore battery optimizations only for apps whose core function breaks otherwise
android.note: While-idle alarms limited to 7 per hour; network and wakelocks suspended except in maintenance windows

ios.note: iOS suspends apps within seconds of backgrounding; no Doze concept; Low Power Mode reduces fetch and push

fields.name: exempt
fields.range: high priority FCM, exact alarm, FGS

limits.headline: Can't force the phone to stay awake; Doze delays jobs, alarms and network
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the phone sits still and unplugged
can: Check if the phone is in idle mode or ignores battery limits
Ask you to exempt it from battery optimization
Run short jobs during maintenance windows on Android
Use Low Power Mode status on iPhone
cannot: Run network jobs while Doze is on, except in maintenance windows
Set more than about 7 alarms per hour while the phone is idle
Avoid iPhone suspending it within seconds of leaving the app
Exempt itself without your choice in Settings
limits.differs: Android has Doze and idle mode. iPhone has no Doze but suspends apps quickly and slows work in Low Power Mode.

story.what_it_is: When your phone sits still and unplugged, Android pauses most app work to save battery.

marketing.name: Doze and App Standby
marketing.pitch: Android saves battery by deferring background work when the device is idle.

story.for_you: You notice it as better battery life overnight. It may also delay a message or an alarm by some minutes. Only high priority messages, exact alarms and some services get through.
story.for_makers: Makers must plan around it: they use high priority push, exact alarms and foreground services for urgent work. Some apps ask users to switch off battery limits, which Google discourages.

use_cases.example: A chat app receives a message through a high priority push while the phone sleeps.
A calendar app rings a meeting alarm on time using an exact alarm.
A step tracker batches data and syncs when the phone wakes.
A game that wants energy refilled uses a timed notification rather than a background job.
A bad app asks you to turn off battery limits so it can keep running at night.
A security camera app uses high priority alerts to wake the phone when motion is seen.

story.android_note: This is Android only, with Doze and App Standby buckets that decide how often an app can run.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no Doze, but it limits background work through its own scheduler.

technical_bounds: FCM high priority is the sanctioned wake path

abuse: Evading Doze with battery opt-out prompts

history.change: Doze on the go (screen off, moving)

refs.label: Android: Optimize for Doze and App Standby
